According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple once considered introducing a feature for the "Apple Upgrade" programme that would make switching to a new iPhone almost seamless: Apple would pre-transfer the user's data. However, the feature ultimately failed to materialise.

The concept is simple: if users upgrade their devices on a regular monthly subscription, why not make the transfer process as simple as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reports as follows:

There are clearly some loopholes. First, your iCloud backup will be slightly out of date, because data transfer can only take place when the device is shipped, which will be a few days later than the actual date, unless you choose to pick it up in person at a store.

In addition, there are obvious privacy concerns. If you use iCloud backups, it should come as no surprise that Apple holds your data. But for the average person, they may be concerned about how the data is transferred to the new phone, and may question whether anyone has peeked at it in the process.

Two years ago, Apple launched a new system called "Presto" in its retail stores, allowing employees to update a device while it was still in the box. It is conceivable that this system could be expanded in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one needing to look at your data throughout the process.

That said, the feature was ultimately never released, and that may actually be a good thing.
